thread_analysis.thread_summary: Premium Audio Company / Klipsch (contacts Munehiro Yoneda, Satoshi Suzuki, Takeshi Kawamura) engages Allion (Yukihiro Nakano, Itsuo Sakai, Toshitaka Mochizuki) for Bluetooth SIG registration of 'THE FIVES' speaker family (representative model The Sevens II plus derivatives The Fives II and The Nines II), spanning March 2025 through December 2025. This is an unusually sophisticated single-thread engagement covering RF test exemption via module design leverage, conditional ICS Mandatory-trigger profile handling, and the full registration-to-Compliance-Folder lifecycle.
all_questions_found: Does the module-design-identity RF test exemption used for Japan Radio Law/FCC/CE certification also apply to Bluetooth SIG certification? (see thread_0052_case_01)
How should an inherited, conditionally-triggered profile requirement (HOGP-driven DIS/SCPP/SCPS) be resolved, and what's the long-term risk of including unused profiles? (see thread_0052_case_02)

(Administrative, not separately cased) Quote/order process with volume-discount coordination across parallel Wi-Fi/HDMI/Bluetooth certification engagements, a SIG login-method change from Username to Email Address (a one-time system transition the customer needed to navigate), the registration public disclosure date's maximum deferral window data point (120 days as of July 21, 2025, since extended further in later threads), model-name formatting consistency across a representative-plus-derivative model family, and the standard Review Page confirmation, registration finalization, and Compliance Folder shipment sequence.
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: Case_01 is among the most sophisticated and previously undocumented technical threads in this corpus, including a notable consultant self-correction: an initial answer (cross-certification-regime test substitution is generally disallowed, requiring full Option 2b re-registration with RF/RF PHY and IOPT testing) was revised after further review to confirm that self-judged antenna-trace design identity alone qualifies for QPRDv3's Option 2a no-additional-testing path. Case_02's conditional ICS Mandatory-trigger explanation and the Withdrawn-profile cascading risk for included-but-unused profiles is a valuable, previously undocumented strategic consideration for any registration that inherits a broader profile set than the actual product uses.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: See thread_0052_case_01 and thread_0052_case_02 for case-specific decision logic.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: See individual case files; case_02's Withdrawn-cascading risk is particularly easy to overlook since it has no immediate consequence at registration time, only surfacing as a blocker if and when an included-but-unused profile is later deprecated.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: Case_01 documents a genuine, transparently-corrected consulting mistake: the initial answer overstated the RF/RF PHY and IOPT testing burden by not fully accounting for the antenna-trace design-identity exemption path, and was promptly revised once reviewed further -- a good example of correcting course rather than letting an overly conservative initial answer stand uncorrected.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When a customer cites a design-identity or test-substitution principle from an adjacent certification regime, investigate the Bluetooth-specific equivalent path thoroughly before concluding it doesn't apply, and be willing to revise an initial answer if subsequent review reveals a more favorable path exists; and when a registration inherits profile requirements beyond what the actual product supports, explain both the no-testing 'Combine Unmodified Design' option and its specific long-term Withdrawn-cascading risk, recommending removal of only the genuinely unused profile when the customer has concrete plans for related future functionality.
